mechanism_narrative: A low federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) reduces the cost of capital for corporations, leading to higher equity valuations and positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are negative in more than 60% of periods when FEDFUNDS is below 4.0% (historical median) over any 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained unemployment rate (UNRATE) above 5.0% signals economic distress and triggers risk-off sentiment, resulting in negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 5-day returns are positive in more than 60% of instances when UNRATE > 5.0% over any 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous decline in labor market growth (PAYEMS) and housing activity (HOUST) signals a broad-based economic slowdown, causing negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are positive in more than 60% of instances when PAYEMS growth is negative and HOUST growth is negative over any 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in industrial production (INDPRO) above 0.5% growth over 3 months signals a strengthening supply sector, leading to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 60-day returns are negative in more than 60% of instances when INDPRO growth > 0.5% over any 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: A housing starts (HOUST) level below 1300.0 thousand units indicates weak residential demand, triggering negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 5-day returns are positive in more than 60% of instances when HOUST < 1300.0 over any 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: A high level of retail sales (RSAFS) indicates strong consumer demand, which supports corporate earnings and leads to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are negative in more than 60% of periods when RSAFS is above historical median (700,000 million dollars) over any 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: A rising inflation rate (CPIAUCSL) above 3.0% per annum signals potential monetary tightening, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are positive in more than 60% of instances when CPIAUCSL > 3.0% over any 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: In a high unemployment regime (UNRATE > 5.0%), a decline in labor market growth (PAYEMS) signals worsening economic conditions, resulting in negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 60-day returns are positive in more than 60% of instances when UNRATE > 5.0% and PAYEMS growth is negative over any 3-year rolling window.
